brief.summary: The supplemental WOTUS comment period closed Oct 9 with no final rule, leaving the scope of federal jurisdiction unsettled. EPA's NPDES definitions proposal remains open until Oct 19, and a Sept 30 CRS update confirms EPA still has no final PFAS effluent guideline after rescinding its state permit guidance in August.
aff: Inherency: CRS confirms no PFAS ELG is final, and the August guidance rescission removes the only federal direction to states on PFAS in permits.
Harms: the 'perennial flow' WOTUS options would take many ephemeral streams and wetlands out of NPDES coverage.
Timing: the Oct 19 NPDES comment deadline shows reform is active but still undecided, so a plan can shape its direction.
neg: Uniqueness: WOTUS, NPDES definitions and PFAS ELGs are all in rulemaking, so the status quo may already deliver reform.
States CP: states hold NPDES authority and can set PFAS limits without federal guidance.
Timeframe: PFAS ELG and permit-application rules are slated for 2027, so the plan may duplicate agency work.

news.title: SBA Office of Advocacy supports additional options for defining "waters of the United States"
news.summary: The SBA's small-business advocate filed comments backing the agencies' September supplemental WOTUS proposal and its narrower jurisdiction options.
news.debate: Neg: small-business compliance-cost evidence against expanding federal jurisdiction. Aff: shows the status quo trend is toward narrower coverage.

news.title: Over 120 organizations oppose Clean Water Act provisions in Senate permitting bill
news.summary: Groups urged Congress to drop CWA language in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, which would narrow state and tribal §401 review, impose a clear-and-convincing burden on denials, and allow 10-year permit terms.
news.debate: Uniqueness: Congress may reform CWA permitting this fall. Aff can claim a different reform; Neg can argue the plan collides with the permitting deal.

news.title: The public waters rollback that "should be avoided at all costs"
news.summary: American Rivers argues the proposed WOTUS rule would leave ephemeral and intermittent streams without federal protection, on top of the wetland losses after Sackett, and urges hunters and anglers to comment before October 9.
news.debate: Aff: harms evidence for narrowing 'navigable waters' — fewer waters means unpermitted discharges. Useful for jurisdiction-restoring affs.

news.title: Regulating PFAS Under the Clean Water Act (CRS In Focus, updated Sept. 30)
news.summary: CRS reports that EPA has finalized no PFAS effluent guideline, that the Organic Chemicals/Plastics/Synthetic Fibers proposal slated for July 2026 and the metal finishing proposal (Feb. 2027) are still pending, and that EPA rescinded its 2022 state NPDES PFAS guidance in August 2026. A rule on PFAS monitoring in permit applications is not expected to be final until about May 2027.
news.debate: Inherency card for Aff: no binding federal PFAS discharge limits exist and the schedule keeps slipping; Neg can cite the pending ELG rulemakings as uniqueness that the plan is already underway.

news.title: EPA pulls guidance on addressing PFAS in wastewater permits
news.summary: EPA rescinded its 2022 memo that gave states model NPDES language for monitoring and limiting PFAS, saying it caused confusion ahead of new effluent guidelines; EWG says states lose a key tool.
news.debate: Aff: inherency for a PFAS effluent-limits plan — no federal PFAS ELGs and now no permit guidance. Neg: states keep full authority to act (states CP).

news.title: New agency WOTUS proposal would eliminate the "wet season" concept
news.summary: EPA and the Army Corps' supplemental proposal would limit jurisdiction to perennial waters and wetlands with a continuous perennial surface connection, adding options to the November 2025 proposal.
news.debate: Uniqueness for both sides: the status quo is actively redefining 'navigable waters', the resolution's key jurisdictional term.

news.title: EPA proposes ending NPDES permit coverage for vessel discharges beyond state waters
news.summary: The proposed rule would redefine "discharge of a pollutant" in 40 CFR 122 so that additions from vessels not secured to the seabed in the contiguous zone (3–12 nm) or ocean need no NPDES permit, citing overlap with MPRSA and VIDA. Comments are due October 19.
news.debate: Topicality and uniqueness: a live federal reform of what counts as a discharge, with seafood processors and seabed mining as named examples. Neg can use it to argue the status quo is already reforming.

news.title: Regulating PFAS under the Clean Water Act (CRS In Focus, updated)
news.summary: CRS reports that EPA has finalized no PFAS effluent guidelines and has not designated any PFAS as a CWA toxic pollutant, and summarizes pending OCPSF, metal finishing and landfill leachate rulemakings.
news.debate: Neutral background card on the PFAS regulatory gap; good for defining what an ELG plan would add.

federal_register.title: Proposed Reissuance of NPDES General Permit for Oil and Gas Exploration Facilities in Federal Waters of Cook Inlet (AKG51000)
federal_register.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Region 10, proposes to reissue the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) General Permit for Oil and Gas Exploration Facilities in Federal Waters of Cook Inlet (draft GP). federal_register.abstract: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps) is seeking input from all interested parties on ways to increase the efficiency of the nationwide permit program. The Corps will consider this input in future rulemaking related to the nationwide permits. The nationwide permits authorize activities under Section 404 of the Clean Water Act and Section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act.

federal_register.title: New Mexico Statewide Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) General Permit Proposal
federal_register.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 6 is providing notice of a proposed National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Statewide general permit for storm water discharges from municipal separate storm sewer systems (MS4s) located in urbanized areas in the State of New Mexico. This permit offers discharge authorization to regulated MS4s within the boundaries of the Bureau of the Census-designated 2000, 2010, and 2020 urbanized area and any other MS4s designated by the Director as needing a MS4 permit.

federal_register.title: New Mexico and Oklahoma Statewide Tribal Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) General Permit Proposal
federal_register.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 6 is providing notice of a proposed National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) statewide general permit for storm water discharges from Tribal municipal separate storm sewer systems (MS4s) located in urbanized areas in the states of New Mexico and Oklahoma. This permit offers discharge authorization to regulated MS4s within the boundaries of the Bureau of the Census-designated 2000, 2010, and 2020 urbanized area and any other MS4s designated by the Director as needing a MS4 permit.

federal_register.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is publishing this proposed rule to update and clarify several substantive and procedural requirements for water quality certification under Clean Water Act (CWA or the Act) section 401. CWA section 401 is a direct grant of authority to States (and Tribes that have been approved for "treatment as a State" status) to review for compliance with appropriate Federal, State, and Tribal water quality requirements any discharge into waters of the United States that may result from a proposed activity that requires a Federal license or permit. federal_register.title: Reissuance and Modification of Nationwide Permits
federal_register.abstract: Nationwide Permits (NWPs) authorize activities under Section 404 of the Clean Water Act and Section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act of 1899 that have no more than minimal individual and cumulative adverse environmental effects. The NWPs help protect the aquatic environment and the public interest by providing incentives to reduce impacts to jurisdictional waters. In this final action, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps) is reissuing 56 existing nationwide permits (NWPs), general conditions, and definitions, with some modifications. The Corps is also issuing one new NWP.
